english_classification.chapter_title: Concerning the Five Storehouses that have poured forth from the Land of Darkness since the [Beginning]; the Five Rulers, the Five Spirits, the Five Bodies, the Five Tastes.
english_classification.chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is dominant in the first two-thirds of this chapter: a systematic five-fold cosmological description of the Kingdom of Darkness, mapping storehouses→elements→trees→genera→worlds, then describing the King of Darkness through zoomorphic forms (lion/eagle/dragon/fish), five properties (darkness/putridity/ugliness/bitterness/burning), three faculties (hardness/magic arts/polyglot knowledge), and further properties (movement/terrifying voice/perceptual limitation). The five sub-king descriptions (¶12-16) each contain pristine substrate (zoomorphic face + metal correspondence + taste correspondence) followed by editorial bridge material applying the cosmic spirit to contemporary institutions ('reigns today in the principalities,' 'sects that worship fire,' 'sites of idols,' 'baptism of the waters,' 'soothsayers'). The editorial fatigue pattern is textbook: +10.29 editorial_bridge drift in the second half. Gardner notes textual development and redactorial confusion about the King of Darkness vs. King of Smoke hierarchy. The substrate's five-fold degree structure (Smoke/Fire/Wind/Water/Darkness → gold/copper/iron/silver/lead → salty/sour/sharp/sweet/bitter → lion/eagle/fish/dragon) is a quintessential correspondential map with both sides internal to the cosmic system.
